title: First Exodus patent and a possible national security hold

tellings.quote:
Some patents apparently go through the
Department of Defense.

plain: A patent for Exodus, the propulsion work that the NASA engineer Charles Buhler describes as antigravity, may have been held up on national security grounds. Buhler, who was part of the work, tells Michels that 'some patents apparently go through the Department of Defense,' and he links this to the Invention Secrecy Act of 1951, a US law that lets the government keep certain patents secret. If so, it would mean the military reviewed or slowed the invention before it could be made public.
